findings.alternative_reading: Earlier positive-definite-loss wording is conditional on identifying interpolation with the zero empirical-loss locus. Literal B.1 assumes absolute boundedness and common population-error Lipschitzness for every distribution, without nonnegativity. Adding nonnegativity excludes this example but does not by itself validate the published exponent.
findings.impact: Major: invalid finite-sample uniform-deviation guarantee as written, used in the core geometry-to-sample-complexity argument. The exact probability5425/131072=0.04138946533203125 exceeds2exp(-5)=0.013475893998170934. The qualitative logarithmic-covering/inverse-square tolerance rate remains repairable.

repair.statement: Safe bound2Nε/(4C)exp(-n ε²/(8D²)) under signed absolute bound; halve uniform-deviation tolerance for ERM excess risk.

findings.core_dependency: Section4.1 Eq4 relates geometry to covering numbers and directs statistical learning to AppendixB. TheoremB.1 Eq13 supplies a uniform-deviation guarantee; Eq14 and pp14-15 combine it with Eq4 for sample-size/ERM claims. The false finite-sample theorem is used in a core geometry-to-sample-complexity derivation.
counterevidence: In the singleton model, ERM excess risk is identically zero; this counterexample does not itself refute the qualitative Eq14 ERM rate or establish learning failure.
Earlier generic noiseless interpolation argument is separate and not refuted.
A safe corrected concentration bound and proper ERM tolerance recover qualitative rate dependence.
The broader algebraic research program and specific nonnegative-loss applications are not shown false.
findings.calibration_basis: The theorem supplies a finite-sample statistical guarantee in the paper's explicit geometric learning argument. This core dependency supports Major; easy correction, a surviving qualitative rate and survival of the broad algebraic program do not alone justify Minor.

scope_clarifications.statement: Specify metric/enclosing scale; bigO normalization ambiguous
Retain activation degree, stride, width and genericity assumptions of cited results
Compact approximation does not imply universal singularity/topology/critical-point preservation; no such theorem asserted

calibration.scope: Targeted severity/dependency reassessment of an existing demonstrated finding; unchanged evidence and no new finding.
calibration.standard: A demonstrated invalid derivation closely tied to a core contribution, or material damage to a core conclusion, normally supports Major. Whole-paper failure, loss of the broad research agenda, or changed benchmark scores is not required. Ease of repair and survival of a qualitative rate do not alone determine severity. Peripheral errors may remain Minor; there is no target count of Major findings.
calibration.standard_origin: Human clarification of intended NeurIPS batch_1 grading standard, applied to the authorized B001 follow-up.
calibration.literal_hypotheses: Real-valued loss from Section3; |ell|<=D; C-Lipschitz population error for every distribution; compact model in the metric. Earlier positive-definite interpolation discussion is conditional, not an explicit B.1 hypothesis.
calibration.controller_confirmation: User reports independent primary-page review, visual inspection ofp14 and exact signed-loss probability confirmation. Existing saved calculation is reused; no fresh Monte Carlo or author-code run.
